Common variations include patch-based discrimination to reduce memory usage and focus on local texture consistency [7571-ganerf.md], gradient penalty terms (e.g., R1 penalty) to stabilize training and prevent mode collapse [7571-ganerf.md], and VGG-based perceptual losses to ensure semantic consistency [7571-ganerf.md].
GNeRF is a two-phase framework that jointly optimizes camera poses and neural radiance fields from uncalibrated images using adversarial training [7359-gnerf.md].
It is designed for scenarios where Structure-from-Motion (SfM) fails due to low texture or complex outside-in configurations [7359-gnerf.md].

Unlike methods requiring rough initialization, GNeRF uses an inversion network to decouple pose estimation from direct photometric gradient propagation, which is prone to local minima [7359-gnerf.md].
It builds on [Radiance-field optimization](44-radiance-field-optimization.md) by introducing a GAN-based generator-discriminator pair [7359-gnerf.md].
GANeRF optimizes a 3D radiance field using a 2D adversarial loss to enforce 3D-consistent photorealism [7571-ganerf.md].
It differs from non-adversarial refinement methods like NeRFLiX by using direct backpropagation from a discriminator to a full-resolution NeRF [7571-ganerf.md].

It builds on [Neural Radiance Fields](4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) by integrating a discriminator into the training loop with adversarial, VGG perceptual, and gradient penalty losses [7571-ganerf.md].
